nde2336d4263.s: A well-tested scientific explanation of why something happens is called a:
nde2336d4263.x: A theory explains why something happens, while a law describes what happens, often mathematically; a theory does not become a law.

nbiology-24-3.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about vitamin K?
o: It is involved in blood clotting
It is needed to make clotting factors
nbiology-24-3.x: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors, so its deficiency increases clotting time and causes bleeding; it does not shorten it.

nbiology-27-3.s: Approximately how much energy does one gram of protein provide?
nbiology-27-3.x: Protein can be burnt for energy and yields about 4 kcal per gram. (No dated facts for a sequence, so a one-liner.)

nbiology-29-13.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the pineal gland?
o: It is located in the brain, in the epithalamus
Its hormone regulates the biological clock
It is located on the kidney
nbiology-29-13.x: The pineal gland sits in the brain (epithalamus) and makes melatonin; the adrenal gland, not the pineal, is located on the kidney.

n3e662acc975.s: How many food irradiators has the Department of Atomic Energy installed in PPP mode?
n3e662acc975.x: DAE has installed 25 food irradiators in PPP mode; gamma rays extend potato and onion shelf life to eight months.

na0ecdd46c44.s: MRI forms images of the body using a strong magnetic field and:
na0ecdd46c44.x: MRI uses a strong magnetic field and radio waves acting on hydrogen nuclei; it uses no ionising radiation.

nfd1d16bf0e5.s: Aarogya Setu carried out COVID-19 contact tracing using:
nfd1d16bf0e5.x: Aarogya Setu used Bluetooth and GPS for COVID-19 contact tracing, not Wi-Fi alone.

nchemistry-17-12.s: Soap is unsuitable for delicate fabrics such as silk and wool because soap solutions are:
nchemistry-17-12.x: Soap hydrolyses to give an alkaline solution, which harms delicate fibres such as silk and wool.

nphysics-16-20.s: The older unit of electrical conductance, the reciprocal of resistance, is the:
nphysics-16-20.x: Conductance G = 1/R, and its older unit is the mho.

nchemistry-6-21.s: Which form of carbon is used in gas masks?
nchemistry-6-21.x: Activated charcoal adsorbs gases in gas masks; diamond is used in glass cutters and graphite as a reactor moderator.

n6dd409c26ad.s: The STI Policy, 2013 envisaged STI intervention in about how many high-impact sectors?
n6dd409c26ad.x: The 2013 policy envisaged STI intervention in about ten high-impact sectors.

n96c173ab7e4.s: One Nation, One Subscription was proposed in which policy?
n96c173ab7e4.x: One Nation, One Subscription came from the Draft STIP 2020 and was approved in 2024; it was not part of the STI Policy, 2013.

n87fcc862af7.s: Which policy aimed to raise GERD to 2% of GDP by the end of the Tenth Plan?
n87fcc862af7.x: The S&T Policy, 2003 set the 2% of GDP GERD target for the end of the Tenth Plan; the 2013 policy repeated 2% with private spending matching public.

ne72c262fd59.s: One Nation, One Subscription was approved by the Cabinet with an outlay of about:
ne72c262fd59.x: The ONOS outlay is about Rs 6,000 crore for 2025-27, not Rs 60,000 crore.

ne3acbee0ece.s: The Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund has an approved size of:
ne3acbee0ece.x: The RDI Fund of Rs 1 lakh crore works through a Special Purpose Fund in ANRF to boost private R&D; Rs 20,000 crore was provided for FY 2025-26.

nab300ea29da.s: The draft National Health Research Policy, 2026 proposes governance with how many tiers?
nab300ea29da.x: The draft, the first unified health-research framework of the Department of Health Research, proposes three-tier governance.

new.s: Science is described as 'know-why'; technology is described as:
new.x: Science is know-why and gives laws and theories; technology is know-how and gives products and processes.

new.s: The first creation of a new product or process is called:
new.x: Invention is the first creation of a product or process; innovation makes it useful in the market or society.

new.s: Research that solves a set problem is called:
new.x: Applied research solves a set problem; basic research is curiosity-driven and translational research takes lab results to use.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about science and technology:
1. The output of science is laws and theories.
2. The output of technology is products and processes.
3. Translational research is curiosity-driven.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Science yields laws and theories and technology yields products and processes; curiosity-driven research is basic research, while translational research takes lab results to use.

new.s: Nanotechnology deals with structures in the size range of:
new.x: Nanotechnology works at 1-100 nanometres.

new.s: In the scientific method, which step comes immediately after experiment?
new.x: The order is observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, conclusion, then replication and peer review.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the scientific method?
o: A hypothesis is framed before the experiment
A well-tested theory finally becomes a law
Replication and peer review follow the conclusion
new.x: A theory explains why and a law describes what happens; a theory does not become a law.

new.s: Statistics is classified among the:
new.x: Formal sciences are mathematics, logic and statistics.

new.s: Geoinformatics combines geography with:
new.x: Geoinformatics is geography plus IT, using GIS, remote sensing and GPS.

new.s: The Earth System Science Organisation (ESSO), set up in 2007, works under:
new.x: ESSO (2007) works under the Ministry of Earth Sciences for ocean, atmospheric, geoscience and polar science.

new.s: On the NASA scale, validation and prototype correspond to Technology Readiness Levels:
new.x: TRL 1-3 runs from basic principles to lab proof of concept, 4-6 is validation and prototype, and 7-9 is operational demonstration and proven use.

new.s: The Technology Readiness Level scale runs from:
new.x: NASA's Technology Readiness Levels run from 1 to 9.

new.s: Identifying a person by gait or signature is an example of:
new.x: Biometrics uses physical traits (fingerprint, iris, face) or behavioural traits (voice, gait, signature).

new.s: A metro smart card works on:
new.x: A metro smart card is a passive NFC card; FASTag is passive RFID.

new.s: Near Field Communication (NFC) works at 13.56 MHz over a range of about:
new.x: NFC works at 13.56 MHz over about 4 cm.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about RFID:
1. It uses radio waves.
2. It needs a line of sight to the reader.
3. FASTag is a passive RFID tag powered by the toll reader.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: RFID uses radio waves and needs no line of sight; FASTag is a passive RFID tag powered by the toll reader.

new.s: Article 51A(h) on scientific temper was added by which Constitutional Amendment?
new.x: Article 51A(h) came with the 42nd Amendment in 1976, not the 86th.

new.s: The Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad, a scientific temper movement, was founded in:
new.x: The Kerala Sastra Sahitya Parishad was founded in 1962; 1981 is the Statement on Scientific Temper.

new.s: Which State passed an Anti-Superstition Act in 2013?
new.x: Maharashtra passed its Anti-Superstition Act in 2013.

new.s: Who popularised the term 'scientific temper' in The Discovery of India?
new.x: Jawaharlal Nehru popularised 'scientific temper' in The Discovery of India.

new.s: India's rank in the Network Readiness Index 2024 was:
new.x: India ranked 49th in the NRI 2024, up from 79th in 2019; 38th is its GII 2025 rank.

new.s: The Giant Metrewave Radio Telescope (GMRT) is located at:
new.x: GMRT, the world's largest metre-wave telescope with 30 dishes, is at Khodad, about 80 km from Pune, not Ooty.

new.s: The Udaipur Solar Observatory is run by:
new.x: PRL, Ahmedabad runs the Udaipur Solar Observatory.

new.s: Which of the following institution–location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: GMRT is at Khodad near Pune; the Ooty Radio Telescope is at Muthorai.

new.s: The Ooty Radio Telescope at Muthorai is run by:
new.x: The Radio Astronomy Centre (Ooty Radio Telescope) at Muthorai belongs to NCRA-TIFR (1969).

new.s: Aristolochic acid, a harmful chemical, is found in:
new.x: Aristolochic acid comes from Aristolochia plants used in some herbal medicines.

new.s: Bisphenol A (BPA) is commonly found in:
new.x: BPA is found in polycarbonate plastics, food-can linings and thermal receipts.

new.s: Phthalates are used mainly as:
new.x: Phthalates are PVC plasticisers found in toys and cosmetics.

new.s: Turmeric is commonly adulterated with:
new.x: Turmeric is adulterated with metanil yellow and lead chromate; argemone oil goes into mustard oil and brick powder into chilli.

new.s: Under the PM Kisan Sampada Yojana Cold Chain scheme, how many irradiation units had been approved by August 2025?
new.x: 16 irradiation units were approved, of which 9 were operational; 25 is the number of DAE irradiators in PPP mode.

new.s: Which preservative is used for dried fruits and in winemaking?
new.x: SO2 preserves dried fruits and is used in winemaking; propionates are used for stored grains and cheese.

new.s: Which preservative is no longer used because it is toxic?
new.x: Boric acid is an old preservative no longer used because it is toxic.

new.s: Deficiency of vitamin B5 (pantothenic acid) causes:
new.x: B5 deficiency causes burning feet; pellagra is due to B3 (niacin) and beri-beri to B1.

new.s: Who coined the term 'vitamine'?
new.x: Casimir Funk coined 'vitamine'; James Lind showed citrus cures scurvy.

new.s: Fat provides about how much energy per gram?
new.x: Fat gives about 9.3 kcal per gram, against about 4 kcal for protein.

new.s: In the human body, urea is made in the:
new.x: Urea is made in the liver and filtered out by the kidney.

new.s: Ultrasound used in medical imaging has a frequency above:
new.x: Ultrasound is sound above 20 kHz; its echoes form images and it is safe for the foetus.

new.s: The Chitra heart valve was developed at SCTIMST, located in:
new.x: SCTIMST, which developed the indigenous Chitra heart valve, is in Thiruvananthapuram.

new.s: Anna Chakra optimises PDS routes to about how many fair price shops?
new.x: Anna Chakra maps PDS routes to 4.37 lakh shops and saves about Rs 250 crore a year.

new.s: An induction cooktop works on:
new.x: An induction cooktop heats by electromagnetic induction and eddy currents; LEDs work on electroluminescence.

new.s: A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water to about:
new.x: Higher pressure raises the boiling point to about 120 C, so food cooks faster.

new.s: In a household circuit, a fuse is connected:
new.x: A fuse works on the heating effect, has a low melting point and is connected in series.

new.s: Besides triggering airbags, MEMS accelerometers are used for:
new.x: MEMS accelerometers trigger airbags, detect laptop free fall and count steps.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a use of hydrogels?
new.x: Hydrogels, up to 99% water, are used in contact lenses, wound dressings, diapers and drug delivery; airbags are triggered by accelerometers.

new.s: C-V2X vehicle communication is based on:
new.x: C-V2X uses 4G/5G; DSRC is the Wi-Fi-based technology.

new.s: The PM E-DRIVE scheme for electric vehicles is run by the:
o: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
new.x: PM E-DRIVE is a scheme of the Ministry of Heavy Industries.

new.s: The PM E-DRIVE scheme has been extended up to:
new.x: PM E-DRIVE has been extended to 31 March 2028.

new.s: Which of the following is a positive impact of technology on daily life?
new.x: Health tracking is a positive impact; decreased privacy, cyber fraud and the digital divide are negative.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the impacts of technology:
1. Flexible work is a positive impact.
2. Eye strain from screen time is a negative impact.
3. Decreased privacy is a positive impact.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Flexible work is positive and screen-time eye strain negative; decreased privacy is a negative impact.

new.s: The Technology Policy Statement, 1983 was issued when the Prime Minister was:
new.x: The Technology Policy Statement, 1983 came under Indira Gandhi.

new.s: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was released under Prime Minister:
new.x: The S&T Policy, 2003 came under Vajpayee; the STI Policy, 2013 came under Manmohan Singh.

new.s: Which policy first added 'Innovation' to India's science and technology policy?
new.x: The STI Policy, 2013 added Innovation with the theme 'STI for the People'.

new.s: The core thrust of the Technology Policy Statement, 1983 was:
new.x: The 1983 statement aimed at technological competence and self-reliance with less import dependence.

new.s: Which of the following policy–Prime Minister pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
new.x: The S&T Policy, 2003 came under Vajpayee; Indira Gandhi issued the Technology Policy Statement, 1983.

new.s: The Science and Technology Policy, 2003 was launched on:
new.x: The S&T Policy, 2003 was launched on 3 January 2003.

new.s: The Atal Innovation Mission was set up in 2016 by:
new.x: AIM was set up by NITI Aayog in 2016; it is not an outcome of the Draft STIP 2020.

new.s: Which financing body was proposed by the Draft STIP 2020?
o: Fund for Innovations for Social Inclusion
new.x: The Draft STIP 2020 proposed an STI Development Bank; the other three belong to the STI Policy, 2013.

new.s: Which two policies set no numeric GERD target?
new.x: The 1958 Resolution and 1983 Statement had no numeric GERD target; the 2% target came with STP 2003.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about India's GERD:
1. It reached 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24.
2. The 2% of GDP goal was met under the STI Policy, 2013.
3. The Draft STIP 2020 proposed doubling GERD every 5 years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: GERD was 0.84% of GDP in FY 2023-24 and STIP 2020 proposed doubling it every 5 years; the 2% goal has been missed under every policy.

new.s: PM-STIAC, set up in 2018, is chaired by the:
new.x: PM-STIAC (2018) is chaired by the Principal Scientific Adviser.

new.s: The Department of Biotechnology was set up in:
new.x: DBT was set up in 1986; DST in 1971, DSIR in 1985 and CSIR in 1942.

new.s: The ANRF outlay of about Rs 50,000 crore covers the period:
new.x: ANRF has about Rs 50,000 crore for 2023-28, of which about Rs 36,000 crore comes from non-government sources.

new.s: Which body was subsumed into the Anusandhan National Research Foundation?
new.x: The ANRF Act 2023 subsumed SERB into ANRF.

new.s: The office of the Principal Scientific Adviser was set up in:
new.x: The PSA office dates from 1999, with A.P.J. Abdul Kalam as the first PSA.

new.s: India's Decade of Innovation covered the period:
new.x: The Decade of Innovation was 2010-2020.

new.s: The National Innovation Council for the Decade of Innovation was headed by:
new.x: The National Innovation Council under Sam Pitroda was the vehicle for the Decade of Innovation, focused on inclusive innovation.

new.s: The SATHI scheme of DST (2020) provides:
new.x: SATHI gives shared high-end analytical instruments; PURSE gives publication-based grants.

new.s: Which DST scheme gives grants to universities based on their publications?
new.x: PURSE gives grants based on publications; FIST upgrades S&T infrastructure.

new.s: The GATI scheme of DST targets:
o: Young students from school to PhD
new.x: GATI is Gender Advancement for Transforming Institutions; Vigyan Jyoti targets schoolgirls.

new.s: Under WISE-KIRAN, the Women Scientists Scheme supports:
new.x: The Women Scientists Scheme under WISE-KIRAN supports career-break women.

new.s: National Science Day on 28 February commemorates the:
new.x: National Science Day marks the Raman Effect (1928).

new.s: National Technology Day on 11 May marks the:
new.x: National Technology Day marks Pokhran-II (1998) and was declared in 1999.

new.s: In the Global Innovation Index 2025, India ranked 38th out of how many economies?
new.x: India ranked 38th of 139 in GII 2025.

new.s: India's rank in the Global Innovation Index 2024 was:
new.x: India was 39th in GII 2024 and rose to 38th in 2025.
